hypothesis: Skipping only the nonessential startup baseline-violation scan, while retaining exact canonical candidate scoring and the pinned evaluator/metric, will allow the documented staged n=7 search to run and may discover a candidate below the frozen primary count of 3.
rationale: Experiments 001 and 002 showed that the generic canonical potential is too slow for the search script's startup scan over 166,681 taxi nodes. The script uses that scan only to append observed baseline violations to an edge-order cache; a conservative all-pinned-edge cache already supplies the startup edge set. Removing this proxy scan is a controlled runtime adaptation, while every candidate’s stage scoring and final result remain exact under the pinned implementation.
expected_information_gain: Tests the scientific staged search family after isolating its startup infrastructure bottleneck, distinguishing candidate-generation performance from baseline-cache throughput.
method: Use research_tools/kserver_n7_search_main.py with exact pinned canonical Potential for every candidate scoring call. When the unmodified staged script requests startup potentials with node_idxes omitted, return a zero-valued ordering proxy and retain the complete pinned edge-index order from build_hard_edge_cache; do not use the proxy for candidate scoring. Link the adapter and pinned checkout into /home/kserver, set fork start semantics, and run the unmodified examples/search_n7_async_pipeline/search_n7_async_pipeline.py with timeout 1800 seconds, n-cpus 20, families seed_dense,mutate_ck4,mutate_proxy,mutate_timed,mutate_full, startup seeds disabled, tag reproduce_n7_codex_proxy. Preserve checkpoints/events and run the exact frozen taxi evaluator on any finalist.
metric: best full circle_taxi_k4_m6 violations_k from exact candidate scoring/evaluator
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A candidate below 3 on the exact pinned primary evaluator is finite benchmark progress toward the k-server objective, not a proof of the full conjecture; the startup proxy affects ordering only and cannot establish a result.

configuration.startup_baseline_scan: zero-valued edge-order proxy; complete pinned edge order retained

kill_condition: Stop at the documented 1800-second search timeout, at the first candidate that passes the exact frozen evaluator and is preserved for verification, or at a precise runtime/contract failure. Do not modify the pinned evaluator or metric.

raw_result.resource_failure: WSL2 global out-of-memory kill during aggregate worker initialization; no search stage result

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if exact evaluator returns violations_k < 3; reproduction at 3 is baseline evidence

previous_best_comparison.previous_pipeline_result: not reached search due adapter cache scalability
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: search-stage result is informative only through exact candidate scoring

interpretation: The startup ordering proxy removed the serial cache bottleneck and reached the controller, but the documented worker configuration exceeded the available WSL memory before any candidate was evaluated.
failure_mode: Aggregate memory exhaustion: six fast workers plus three heavy workers were initialized under a 7.6 GiB no-swap WSL instance; the kernel killed a Python process with approximately 2.1 GiB anonymous RSS.
what_was_learned: This configuration cannot run on the available local runtime. The failure occurred before stage-A completion, so it gives no information about candidate quality or the mathematical objective.
recommended_next_action: Run one resource-capped wrapper experiment with one fast worker, one worker per heavy stage, and one nested process per heavy worker; preserve the upstream search and exact pinned scoring. If that also fails before useful scoring, pause k-server work pending more capable compute or the missing reported candidate.
repetition_justification: This is a justified third attempt after two distinct adapter scalability failures. The changed condition is narrowly limited to the startup edge-order proxy; exact candidate scoring, pinned evaluator, metric, search families, seed, and mathematical target remain unchanged.
